threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use the word 'tube' to refer to public transport. Everyone here calls it 'the Overground' or just 'the train' now.
Last week on the 36, a guy argued with a pigeon over a seat. The pigeon won, strutting around like it owned the bus. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy busking with a parrot on his shoulder outside Reuterstraße, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand open at 4 AM serving fresh döner to clubbers, while the U-Bahn is still on strike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals rush to the bodega for a michelada when they hear the BART alarm. It's like, the only band-aid for a broken commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a whiff of burnt rubber on the Civic Center platform today. Turns out, it was just another dog munching on snacks left behind. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that the best vermut spots aren’t on the main streets—they’re tucked away in small plazas, where locals sip slowly and chat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the 5-minute wait for the next tram at Plaça de la Vila; locals know it’s just how it is.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'Islington' instead of 'Is-lin-ton' and don't know which end of Kingsland Road has the best late-night kebabs.
Last Saturday, the 45 bus had a guy singing opera at the back. Made the bumpy ride home feel like a late-night concert. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid selling handmade bracelets on Karl-Marx-Straße while a street musician played Beethoven. That's Neukölln life for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find people dancing with their dogs at the weekend flea market on Boxhagener Platz. It's just a typical Sunday here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they avoid the Civic Center Muni stop at all costs, especially when a dog takes over the tracks. It's a whole vibe.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The other day, a clown on a unicycle stopped the Muni at Larkin. Everyone laughed, but we were still late to work. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for hip cafes, but they miss the bustling local markets where the real food stories unfold.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle with the metro card machines—seems like it takes forever to figure out that '28' means a 10-ride pass.
